chunks: With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Haytham ibn Abdullah al-Nahdi, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Manliness is two types: the manliness of the settled one, and the manliness of the traveler. As for the manliness of the settled one, it is recitation of the Qur'an, attending mosques, accompanying the people of goodness, and contemplation in jurisprudence. And as for the manliness of the traveler, it is providing provisions, joking in that which does not anger Allah, little dispute with the one who accompanies you, and abandoning narrating their faults when you depart from them.

key_terms.الْمُرُوءَةُ: Manliness, virtue, or nobility of character
key_terms.مُرُوءَةُ الْحَضَرِ: The manliness/virtue of the settled person (at home)

ai.seo_question: What are the two types of manliness (muru'ah) in Shia ethics according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishing between the spiritual discipline of the settled believer—marked by Quranic recitation and jurisprudential study—and the social etiquette of the traveler, emphasizing generosity and conflict avoidance. This dichotomy reflects the Shia emphasis on adapting virtuous conduct (*akhlaq*) to one's specific context, ensuring that religious obligations are balanced with practical social harmony during journeys.
